text.p: French September bond futures ended higher, supported by the U.S. bond market which maintained its gains on Thursday after solid rises on Wednesday, despite a rise in the Philadelphia Fed index, dealers said.
"We're benefitting from the upturn in the T-bond. Without that the European markets would undoubtedly have been lower," a trader said.
"There is a bit of a feeling of euphoria in the market, albeit with small volumes, which is hiding the risks that still linger in Europe," another dealer said.
In the United States, fears of a possible rise the Fed funds rate seem to have waned after a Philadelphia Fed report said economic activity was solid but non-inflationary.
The index, published in the afternoon, showed a rise to 28.1 from 25.2 in June.
Other U.S. indicators today were unemployment benefits and housing starts. They were in line with expectations and did not have an impact on the market, dealers said.
The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds fell to 6.47 percent, its lowest since December.
The notionnel followed this movement, "forgetting that on this side of the Atlantic, there is a potential for bad news," a trader said.

In France, two experts of the Court of Auditors will present their report on the public finances to the new Socialist-led government on Monday. It will be published the same day and could show a deficit of 3.5 to 3.6 percent of GDP.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin chaired a meeting of ministers on Thursday to discuss how to tackle the budget in the event of a shortfall. Spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said no decisions had been taken.
Asked whether the government was considering a new austerity plan to bring down the deficit, Trautmann said, "No, it is out of the question".

The government has said it will take action to curb the budget deficit if needed but has ruled out new austerity just to meet a strict interpretation of Maastricht treaty criteria on monetary union. It is expected to use a mix of tax increases on companies and the rich and savings to bring down the deficit.
The franc traded at 3.3786/88 against the mark, versus 3.3766/68 on Wednesday. The dollar came back below the 1.800 level against the mark at ended at 1.7918/28.
